raw_segments.text: Bessie invited him to walk into the breakfast room and led the way out.
In the interview which followed between him and Mrs. Reed, I presume, from after occurrences,
that the apothecary ventured to recommend my being sent to school, and the recommendation
was no doubt readily enough adopted.
For as Abbott said, in discussing the subject with Bessie when both sat sewing in the nursery
one night, after I was in bed, and as they thought asleep, Mrs. was, she dared say,
glad enough to get rid of such a tiresome, ill-conditioned child who always looked as
if she were watching everybody and scheming plots under hand.
Abbott, I think, gave me credit for being a sort of infant and guy fox.
